mechanism_narrative: The recent rebound in WORKPLACES from -22.7 to -3.4 implies more commuting and weekday foot traffic, which should lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks relative to the last four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved sharply from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES does not stay above its recent trough and RETAIL_REC does not average higher over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in TRANSIT below its recent range signals weaker shared transport access to shopping districts, which should push RETAIL_REC lower within two weeks and keep it below the prior four-week mean.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -20 and remains there for at least one weekly mean
failure_condition: If TRANSIT recovers above -20 quickly and RETAIL_REC does not fall below its last-4-week average within 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated while WORKPLACES stay depressed, people substitute toward local, convenience-oriented trips and avoid discretionary retail, reducing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed positive while WORKPLACES was negative in every week shown
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains above baseline but RETAIL_REC rises instead of falling over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained improvement in PARKS mobility indicates favorable outdoor conditions and wider weekend movement, which spills into discretionary shopping and raises RETAIL_REC over the next two to four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 10 points from one weekly mean to the next
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -18.9 to -8.3 between t-2w and t-1w
failure_condition: If PARKS improves by 10+ points but RETAIL_REC does not increase above its prior four-week mean within 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: If grocery-and-pharmacy mobility turns positive while transit remains weak, retail demand shifts toward essential trips instead of discretionary shopping, holding RETAIL_REC down over the next month.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM is above 0 while TRANSIT is below -10
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM was positive in two of the last three weeks
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM stays positive and TRANSIT stays below -10 but RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week average.

mechanism_narrative: A short-run recovery in RETAIL_REC itself tends to persist because shopping trips are habit-forming and respond with a one-week lag to prior footfall patterns, so a current trough should be followed by a higher four-week average.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -14.7 to -9.0 before easing to -10.6
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to improve within one week after a recent local low and remains below the last-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES rebounds while TRANSIT remains suppressed, commuting shifts toward private or remote arrangements rather than shopping-oriented travel, so the retail rebound is delayed and RETAIL_REC stays below trend for four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -10 while TRANSIT stays below -15
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rebounded sharply at t-0w while TRANSIT stayed negative
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES rises above -10 and TRANSIT stays below -15 but RETAIL_REC still averages higher than in the previous four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A synchronized rise in GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS marks broader out-of-home activity and neighborhood circulation, which should spill into retail visits and raise RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS both improved relative to their lows in the snapshot
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS rise together but RETAIL_REC does not improve within 14 days.
